The '''2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 13 December 2020<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishcentral.com/sports/gaa-all-ireland-2020|title=GAA confirms plans for this year's Inter-County Football and Hurling Championships|date=June 26, 2020|website=IrishCentral.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-december-all-ireland-5133792-Jun2020/|title=December All-Ireland final dates confirmed as GAA unveil 2020 championship plan|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole|website=The42}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/all-ireland-finals-set-for-december-13th-and-19th-as-gaa-confirm-2020-schedule-1.4289406|title=All-Ireland finals set for December 13th and 19th as GAA confirm 2020 schedule|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan|newspaper=The Irish Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/2020-all-ireland-senior-hurling-championship-key-dates-1.4289497|title=2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship key dates|first=Seán|last=Moran|newspaper=The Irish Times}}</ref> between [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] and [[Waterford county hurling team|Waterford]], the culmination of the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|133rd final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]].

Limerick won the game by 0–30 to 0–19 to claim their second All-Ireland title in three years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/gaa-hurling-all-ireland-senior-championship/limerick-waterford/1739657/|title=LIMERICK 0-30 WATERFORD 0-19|date=13 December 2020|work=GAA.ie|accessdate= 11 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2020/1213/1184174-all-ireland-shc-final-limerick-v-waterford-build-up/|title=All-Ireland SHC final recap: Limerick 0-30 Waterford 0-19|date=13 December 2020|work=RTE Sport|accessdate= 11 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/live-all-ireland-hurling-final-limerick-0-30-waterford-0-19-ft-1.4435608|title=LIVE All-Ireland hurling final: Limerick 0-30 Waterford 0-19 (FT)|date=13 December 2020|work=Irish Times|accessdate= 11 May 2021}}</ref>

The match was televised live on RTÉ2 as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]] from the outside studio at Croke Park, with analysis by [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Donal Óg Cusack]] and [[Henry Shefflin]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The match was also live on [[Sky Sports]], with analysis from [[Jamesie O'Connor]] and [[Ollie Canning]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-waterford-all-ireland-hurling-final-live-score-updates-5298330-Dec2020/|title=Limerick 0-30 Waterford 0-19: As it happened|date=13 December 2020|work=The 42|accessdate= 11 May 2021}}</ref>

==Background==
*The championship was delayed due to the [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Gaelic games]]. This was the latest the final had taken place in a year since [[1924 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1924]], when the All-Ireland hurling final took place on 14 December.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-31008354.html|title=Own points and unfinished matches: The story of hurling championship games in December|first=Leo|last=McGough|date=June 30, 2020|website=Irish Examiner}}</ref>
*Waterford had not won the All-Ireland since [[1959 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1959]] (61 years) and had only appeared in three finals in the interim ([[1963 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1963]], [[2008 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2008]] and [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2017]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cyril-farrell-triedandtrusted-waterford-gameplan-will-rattle-galway-36028648.html|title=Cyril Farrell: Tried-and-trusted Waterford game-plan will rattle Galway|date=14 August 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=14 August 2017}}</ref>
*This was the third final in the previous four years not to involve one of the [[Big Three (hurling)|Big Three]] (Cork, Kilkenny, Tipperary) — the [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2017]] (Galway—Waterford) and [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2018]] (Limerick—Galway) finals also did not involve them.
*This was the third final in which both the teams were from the province of Munster, with the first two being in [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1997]] (Clare—Tipperary) and [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2013]] (Clare—Cork).
*This was only the third All-Ireland final in history in which neither team scored a goal, the first two being in 1999 and 2004.

==Pre-match==
The [[2020 Joe McDonagh Cup final]] between [[Kerry county hurling team|Kerry]] and [[Antrim county hurling team|Antrim]] took place prior to the All-Ireland senior final.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40186725.html|title= Antrim and Kerry hurlers may not watch All-Ireland final at Croke Park |date=8 December 2020|work=Irish Examiner|access-date= 9 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40189899.html|title=Antrim see off Kerry to secure McDonagh Cup success at Croke Park |date=13 December 2020|work=Irish Examiner|access-date= 16 December 2020}}</ref>

On 4 December 2020, the officials were chosen for the final by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]], with Tipperary's [[Fergal Horgan]] being named as the referee in what would be his second senior final after being the referee in [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2017]]. Colm Lyons from Cork was named as standby referee, with the other linesman being Paud O'Dwyer from Carlow and the sideline official Seán Cleere from Kilkenny.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40148969.html|title= Fergal Horgan confirmed as All-Ireland Hurling final referee|date=4 December 2020|work=Irish Examiner|access-date= 9 December 2020}}</ref>

===Jubilee team===
The [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]] team that won the [[1995 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1995 All-Ireland Final]] were remembered before the match to mark 25 years. There was no traditional walk out and parade due to [[COVID-19]] restrictions but the Clare captain of 1995 [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]] was present to place the Liam MacCarthy Cup in front of the Hogan Stand before the match.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/anthony-daly-to-represent-clare-jubilee-team-on-all-ireland-day/|title=Anthony Daly to represent Clare jubilee team on All-Ireland day|date=6 January 2021|work=GAA.iel|access-date= 6 January 2021}}</ref>

==Post-match==
''[[Financial Times]]'' columnist [[Simon Kuper]] wrote after [[Stephen O'Keeffe]]'s performance that hurling was "the best sport ever and if the Irish had colonised the world, nobody would ever have heard of [[Association football|football]]".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Article/Index/314775|title=GAA tweets of the week|work=Hogan Stand|date=14 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://twitter.com/KuperSimon/status/1338150109440323584|title=Tweet by Simon Kuper}}</ref>
